mcqs.question: In a standard electrocardiogram (ECG) tracing, which of the following descriptions correctly identifies the QRS complex?

options.A: A small upward deflection that appears before the P wave
options.B: A sharp, large deflection consisting of a brief downward (Q) wave followed by a tall upward (R) wave and a small downward (S) wave, representing ventricular depolarisation
options.C: A modest upward wave occurring after the QRS complex, representing ventricular repolarisation
options.D: A flat isoelectric line with no deflection

mcqs.answer: A sharp, large deflection consisting of a brief downward (Q) wave followed by a tall upward (R) wave and a small downward (S) wave, representing ventricular depolarisation
mcqs.explanation: The QRS complex is the prominent, sharp set of waves (Q, R, S) that reflects the rapid depolarisation of the ventricles. Option B describes this correctly. Option A describes a pre‑P activity, which does not exist. Option C describes the T wave, and option D is the baseline.

mcqs.question: An ECG strip shows a modest upward deflection that follows the QRS complex and returns to the baseline. Which wave is shown?
mcqs.explanation: The T wave appears after the QRS complex and represents ventricular repolarisation. It is usually a broader, modest upward deflection. The P wave precedes the QRS, the Q wave is part of the QRS complex, and the U wave (if present) follows the T wave.

mcqs.learning_point: Relate ECG components to cardiac events
mcqs.question: Match each ECG component with the cardiac event it represents:

options.A: P wave – atrial depolarisation; QRS complex – ventricular depolarisation; T wave – ventricular repolarisation
options.B: P wave – ventricular repolarisation; QRS complex – atrial depolarisation; T wave – atrial repolarisation
options.C: P wave – atrial repolarisation; QRS complex – ventricular repolarisation; T wave – ventricular depolarisation
options.D: P wave – atrial depolarisation; QRS complex – atrial repolarisation; T wave – ventricular depolarisation

mcqs.answer: P wave – atrial depolarisation; QRS complex – ventricular depolarisation; T wave – ventricular repolarisation
mcqs.explanation: The P wave corresponds to the depolarisation of the atria, the QRS complex to the rapid depolarisation of the ventricles, and the T wave to the repolarisation of the ventricles. The other options mix up the sequence of events.

mcqs.question: A technician places electrodes on a patient’s limbs and records voltage changes over time. Which principle underlies the generation of the ECG trace displayed on the monitor?

options.A: Measurement of blood pressure fluctuations in the arteries
options.B: Detection of electrical potentials generated by the heart’s muscular activity as they propagate to the body surface
options.C: Recording of acoustic sounds produced by heart valves
options.D: Visualization of blood flow velocity using Doppler effect

mcqs.answer: Detection of electrical potentials generated by the heart’s muscular activity as they propagate to the body surface
mcqs.explanation: An ECG records the electrical activity produced by the depolarisation and repolarisation of cardiac muscle cells. Electrodes detect these potentials on the skin. Options A, C, and D describe unrelated physiological measurements.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements about the P wave on an ECG is correct?
mcqs.explanation: The P wave is the first small upward deflection on an ECG and corresponds to the depolarisation of the atria. Ventricular depolarisation is shown by the QRS complex, and ventricular repolarisation by the T wave. Atrial repolarisation is not usually visible as a separate wave.

mcqs.question: A trace shows a large, sharp deflection lasting about 0.09 seconds with a high amplitude, occurring after a small P wave. Which component does this describe?
mcqs.explanation: The QRS complex is characteristically large, sharp, and of short duration (0.06–0.10 s). Its appearance after the P wave matches the description. The P wave is smaller and precedes the QRS; the T and U waves occur later and are broader.

mcqs.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes the T wave from the P wave on an ECG?

options.A: The T wave occurs before the QRS complex, whereas the P wave occurs after it
options.B: The T wave is always negative in lead II, while the P wave is always positive
options.C: The T wave represents atrial repolarisation, whereas the P wave represents ventricular depolarisation
options.D: The T wave follows the QRS complex and represents ventricular repolarisation, while the P wave precedes the QRS complex and represents atrial depolarisation

mcqs.answer: The T wave follows the QRS complex and represents ventricular repolarisation, while the P wave precedes the QRS complex and represents atrial depolarisation
mcqs.explanation: Option D accurately describes the temporal order and physiological meaning of the two waves. Options A, B, and C contain incorrect statements about timing, polarity, or the cardiac events represented.

mcqs.learning_point: Relate ECG components to cardiac events
mcqs.question: In a typical ECG, which sequence correctly matches the wave/segment with the cardiac event it reflects?

options.A: P wave – ventricular repolarisation; PR segment – atrial depolarisation; QRS complex – atrial repolarisation
options.B: P wave – atrial repolarisation; ST segment – ventricular depolarisation; T wave – atrial depolarisation
options.C: P wave – atrial depolarisation; QRS complex – ventricular depolarisation; T wave – ventricular repolarisation
options.D: P wave – atrial depolarisation; QRS complex – ventricular repolarisation; ST segment – atrial repolarisation

mcqs.answer: P wave – atrial depolarisation; QRS complex – ventricular depolarisation; T wave – ventricular repolarisation
mcqs.explanation: Option C correctly aligns each ECG component with its physiological event. The PR segment is a period of conduction between atrial and ventricular depolarisation, not a depolarisation itself. The ST segment reflects the plateau phase of ventricular depolarisation, not a separate wave. All other options misassign events.
